title: Carry the wheel to the basket (Unitree G1, walking, Pink IK)
text:
Two heavy-duty packing tables stand 3.0 m apart, their tops 0.69 m off the floor. On the near table a car steering wheel about 29 cm across lies flat, hub up. The far table carries an open plastic basket, its rim 0.78 m up and its interior about 70 x 46 cm — roomy enough to take the wheel lying flat. Nothing stands between the two tables but open floor.
Goal: pick the steering wheel up off the near table, carry it to the far table, and put it in the basket. The task is complete once the wheel is resting inside the basket, released and come to rest — not still held, not balanced on the rim.
The two tables are further apart than any arm reaches, so the wheel can only get there if the robot itself does.
success: Success, exactly (floor frame: origin at the robot's start spot, +y straight ahead toward the near table, +x to its right toward the far table, z up): (a) at some moment the steering wheel's origin, which starts 5.6 mm above the near table top with the wheel flat, rose above 0.744 m (5 cm above the 0.694 m table top). (b) At or after that moment, the origin was more than 2.70 m to the right (x > 2.7 m, 90% of the 3.0 m table-to-table offset). (c) At the end, the wheel's origin is inside the basket target zone: x between 3.40 and 3.85 m, y between 0.35 and 0.60 m (an inset within the basket's ~0.70 x 0.46 m interior), and height below 1.100 m (0.406 m above the far table top). Every component of its linear (m/s) and angular (rad/s) velocity is under 0.20. Not true at the start.
